channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan National Bank Joins Basel Consultative Group for Banking Regulation
item.description: The National Bank of Tajikistan has become a member of the Basel Consultative Group (BCG), an international platform for dialogue on banking regulation and supervision. This move aims to strengthen international cooperation, adopt international best practices, and implement modern standards within Tajikistan's banking system. Membership allows for early discussion of the Basel Committee's initiatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Private Pension Fund Manager 'Sentras Securities' Sees Significant Asset Growth
item.description: Kazakhstan's private pension fund manager, 'Sentras Securities', has significantly increased its share of pension assets under management, reaching 25.3%. The company's managed assets grew from 4.4 billion to 68 billion tenge since the beginning of the year. The National Bank still manages the largest portion of pension assets.

item.title: World Bank: Over Half of Kyrgyzstan's Workforce Engaged in Informal Sector
item.description: More than half of Kyrgyzstan's working population is employed in the informal sector, according to the World Bank. In 2023, 56% of citizens worked unofficially in their primary employment. This high level of informal employment hinders private business development, limiting access to credit, formal contracts, and investments for businesses and social protection for workers.

item.title: Former Akym Karim Kokirekbaev, Jailed for Bribery, May Be Released Early Due to Illness
item.description: Former Akym of Zhambyl region, Karim Kokirekbaev, has been released from serving his sentence due to severe illness. However, the prosecution has appealed the court's decision, seeking its annulment. Kokirekbaev was convicted in July 2025 for accepting a large bribe, causing 1.9 billion tenge in damages. He served as Akym from 2013-2018.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Banning E-Scooter Rentals for Under-18s, Increasing Operator Liability
item.description: A parliamentary committee in Kyrgyzstan has approved a bill in its first reading to ban e-scooter rentals for individuals under 18 and enhance the responsibility of rental companies. The Ministry of Internal Affairs noted the bill needs further refinement as it only addresses rentals, not privately owned scooters. The initiative aims to improve road safety and regulate rental services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Aim to Boost Bilateral Trade to $3 Billion by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan plan to increase their bilateral trade volume to $3 billion by 2030, according to the Ministry of Economy and Commerce. The issue was discussed during a meeting between Minister Bakyt Sydykov and Kazakhstan's Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, Abylkair Skakov. Trade turnover between the two countries grew 2.3 times from 2021-2025.

item.title: 11 fire engines in Ulytau region deemed unusable due to akimat negligence
item.description: Eleven units of fire fighting equipment in the Ulytau region are unusable due to the negligence of local executive bodies (akimats). The prosecutor's office reported that proper measures were not taken to maintain the equipment, leading to 11 out of 20 units being inoperable.

item.title: Ecologists assess Almaty SuperSki site, finding no threat to rare species or glaciers
item.description: Kazakh scientists have assessed the Almaty SuperSki resort construction site, concluding it will not harm habitats of rare animals or endangered plants, including the Sievers apple tree. Studies also indicate no significant impact on glaciers, water resources, or soil.

item.title: Barcelona's Lamine Yamal to Miss Champions League Match Against Sabah Due to Ankle Discomfort
item.description: Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal will miss the Champions League match against Azerbaijani club Sabah due to discomfort in his right ankle. The decision was made as a precautionary measure, with Yamal expected to be available for the upcoming league match.

item.title: Three Impersonators Arrested in Kyrgyzstan for Extorting 300,000 Som
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security has arrested three individuals posing as police officers in the Jayyl district. The suspects allegedly extorted 300,000 Kyrgyz som from a citizen by impersonating officers from the local police department.

item.title: New Study on Workplace Violence and Harassment Presented in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Results of a nationwide study on violence and harassment in the workplace were presented in Kyrgyzstan. The study, conducted by CAS Analytics with support from the Insan-Leilek Foundation and the Solidarity Center, was presented at a meeting of the Council for Women's and Children's Rights.

item.title: Former lawyer alleges extortion and fraud at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University
item.description: A former lawyer for Sherzat Polat has raised concerns about alleged extortion and fraud at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University. He claims student groups, possibly linked to university administration, are pressuring students for money. The lawyer is investigating potential violations of Article 190 of the Criminal Code (fraud) and urges students and parents to report such incidents.

item.title: Finland to share geological data management expertise with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will collaborate with Finland to enhance geological data management and digitalization in the resource sector. Deputy Minister AmanTur Tursuniazov met with Finnish Geological Survey representatives to discuss the DATA4CRM project. This cooperation aims to improve data quality, accessibility, and modernize resource management practices.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Water Saving Over Siberian River Diversion Project
item.description: Uzbekistan's Water Minister Shavkat Khamraev stated that water-saving technologies are more economically viable than participating in a $100 billion Siberian river diversion project. The country already saves 11 billion cubic meters of water annually through infrastructure modernization, a figure comparable to the proposed project's diversion volume. Further investments in water conservation are deemed more cost-effective.

item.title: Bishkek to Host Job Fair Offering Over 4,000 Vacancies for Youth
item.description: A job fair for youth will be held in Bishkek on November 26, featuring over 40 employers offering more than 4,000 job openings. The event, organized by the Ministry of Labor, Social Security, and Migration, will take place at the International University of Kyrgyzstan. Positions will be available in IT, law, education, journalism, and management.

item.title: Administrative Barriers Hinder Investment Project Realization in Kazakhstan
item.description: Administrative barriers and unclear responsibilities among government bodies are impeding the timely realization of investment projects in Kazakhstan. A deputy noted that while no projects are complete failures, many face delays in commissioning and reaching full capacity due to these systemic issues and time losses.

item.title: Turonbank Comments on Reports of CEO's Detention
item.description: Turonbank's press service has commented on reports regarding the detention of its head, Chori Mirzaev, on suspicion of large-scale embezzlement. The bank assures that operations continue as usual, with all services and platforms functioning normally. Previous obligations to clients and partners remain valid.

item.title: Kazakh Tenge Weakens Sharply Against US Dollar Amid Global Market Volatility
item.description: The Kazakh tenge has fallen below 455 against the US dollar, its weakest point in a short period. Factors contributing to this include falling oil prices, a sell-off in US stock markets, and investors moving away from riskier assets. Increased domestic demand for currency also pressured the tenge, according to the Association of Financiers of Kazakhstan.

item.title: Energy Facilities Inspected in Kyrgyzstan's Naryn Region
item.description: The operations of the Naryn electricity network enterprise were inspected. First Deputy Director Bakyt Zholdoshbekov reviewed the condition of energy facilities, including substations in Jumgal and Kochkor districts. Special attention was paid to ensuring the uninterrupted and reliable operation of energy facilities and the quality of ongoing work.

item.title: Uzbekistan Tax Committee Denies Data Leak from Its Systems
item.description: The State Tax Committee of Uzbekistan has stated that its information systems were not hacked, refuting claims of a data leak from online cash register systems. Preliminary findings suggest the incident is linked to the infrastructure of an online cash register operator. The committee is investigating whether the operator adhered to information security requirements.

item.title: Foreigners May Be Entrusted with Managing Special Economic Zones in Kazakhstan
item.description: There is a possibility that foreigners could be entrusted with the management of Special Economic Zones (SEZs) within Kazakhstan. This potential shift in management could impact the operational and strategic direction of these economic zones. Further details regarding the scope and implications of such a decision are anticipated.

item.title: China and Central Asia Expand Cooperation at Tashkent Forum
item.description: China and Central Asian nations are broadening cooperation across various sectors, including transport, technology, green energy, and research. Discussions at a Tashkent international forum focused on high-quality Belt and Road Initiative development and green innovation. Academic exchanges and youth programs were highlighted as crucial for mutual understanding and future relations.

item.title: Land Dispute in Kunar Province Results in One Fatality
item.description: The Taliban security command in Kunar province reported that one person was killed in a land dispute between two families in the Wata Pur district. The incident occurred on Monday morning. Taliban forces surrounded the area and arrested five individuals suspected of involvement. Details about the families involved and the exact circumstances of the conflict were not fully disclosed.

item.title: CIS Countries to Develop Unified Rules for Marketplaces and Digital Platforms
item.description: A meeting of the CIS Parliamentary Assembly's Permanent Commission on Legal Issues was held in Turkmenistan to discuss a draft model law regulating digital platforms and marketplaces. The law aims to define the responsibilities of digital platform owners and operators. Participants included representatives from Armenia, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Russia.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Construction Material Production Worth 975 Billion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Industry and Construction aims to increase the share of domestic building materials to 80% of the market. Current domestic production already meets 73% of demand. The ministry has identified 98 investment projects totaling 975 billion tenge, which are expected to significantly boost the sector and increase the availability of local products within the next three years.

item.title: Kazakhstan Rises to 16th in UN E-Government Development Index, Entering Top Tier
item.description: Kazakhstan has climbed to 16th place in the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI), marking its first entry into the highest rating class. This significant advancement, noted as one of the most substantial among leading countries, positions Kazakhstan among nations like South Korea, Denmark, and the USA. The country's EGDI score improved to 0.9363.

item.title: The Guardian Assesses Sindarov's Chances in World Championship Match
item.description: The Guardian highlights the upcoming World Chess Championship match between Sindarov and Gukesh as the youngest in 140 years. Sindarov, ranked fourth globally, holds a significant rating advantage over Gukesh. He also leads in their head-to-head classical and rapid games, making him a favored contender.

item.title: Head of Testing Center Explains Why ORT Should Remain Independent
item.description: The director of Kyrgyzstan's Education Assessment and Methods Center explains that transferring the national testing (ORT) to a state institution could increase the risk of administrative pressure on results. She cited instances of high-ranking officials attempting to influence scores, emphasizing the need for equal testing conditions for all applicants.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Extensive Oil Exploration, Potential Billions of Tons
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to launch a large-scale geological exploration program from 2026 to 2030, aiming to discover billions of tons of oil. The program includes seismic surveys and drilling 26 exploratory wells, with a potential resource of 4.7 billion tons of conditional fuel. Efforts are also underway to increase gas production and expand refinery capacities.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 10 Trillion Tenge Industrial Support Under Scrutiny for Effectiveness
item.description: Questions have been raised about the effectiveness of state support for Kazakhstan's manufacturing industry. Despite 10 trillion tenge allocated since 2010, the sector's share in GDP only increased by 1.5 percentage points. A deputy highlighted systemic issues hindering further development, questioning if the growth is commensurate with the massive state investment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers New Rules for Online Platforms to Combat Counterfeit Goods
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Justice proposes new regulations for e-commerce platforms like Kaspi, Wildberries, and Ozon. These rules aim to streamline the process for intellectual property rights holders to report violations. If adopted, platforms could temporarily suspend sales of disputed goods upon receiving a complaint, while allowing sellers to contest the suspension.

item.title: Tajikistan Proposes Increasing Quotas for Higher Education in Russia
item.description: Tajikistan has proposed increasing educational quotas for its citizens studying in Russian universities and organizing targeted training for pedagogical staff. The initiative aims to align specialized training with Tajikistan's national education system needs and labor market demands, focusing on priority sectors and teaching professions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Online Theory Exam for Driver's Licenses
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced an online option for taking the theoretical driver's license exam through the eGov Mobile app. This new service allows citizens to complete the test remotely without visiting a Public Service Center (TsON), saving time and offering convenience. The option to take the exam in person at a TsON remains available.

item.title: Gold prices in Uzbekistan drop significantly, reaching multi-month low
item.description: Gold prices in Uzbekistan have fallen by nearly 5%, reaching their lowest level in months. The Central Bank reported that a five-gram gold bar now costs 8.483 million soms, a decrease of 418,000 soms from the previous Friday. The price per gram has dropped to 1.697 million soms, influenced by global market price reductions.

item.title: One-Year Restriction Imposed on Vehicle Traffic at "Chaldybar" Border Crossing
item.description: The State Border Service announced a temporary one-year restriction on vehicle traffic at the "Chaldybar - Avtodor" crossing point on the Kyrgyz-Kazakh border. The restriction, effective November 25, prohibits light vehicles, trucks, and buses from crossing in both directions due to construction at Kazakhstan's "Sypatai Batyr - Avtodor" crossing. Pedestrian crossings remain unaffected.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Oil Company Reports on Ten Months of Operations
item.description: Kazakhstan's national oil company, KazMunayGas, presented its operational results for the first ten months of the year. The company's capital stands at 22 trillion tenge, enabling significant investment projects. Plans include geological exploration and drilling to boost gas production and develop new export routes.

item.title: EU Criticizes Tajikistan for Hosting Putin Amid ICC Arrest Warrant
item.description: The European Union expressed regret that Tajikistan hosted Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant. The EU stated that Tajikistan, a signatory to the Rome Statute, failed to fulfill its obligations by not arresting Putin during his November visit.

item.title: Chaldybar Border Crossing Between Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan to Close Temporarily
item.description: The Chaldybar border crossing point between Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan will be temporarily closed to all transport from November 25 due to major construction at the adjacent Kazakh checkpoint. Pedestrian traffic will continue as normal. The closure is expected to last until the end of 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tenge Weakens Amid Falling Oil Prices and US Market Downturn
item.description: The Kazakhstani Tenge has weakened due to declining oil prices and the situation in the US stock market. The USD/KZT exchange rate reached 455.32 tenge per dollar, an increase of 6.19 tenge. Trading volume hit a record $825.6 million. Experts cite external factors like falling oil prices and a global trend of investors divesting from risky assets.

item.title: Tajikistan Sees Decline in Births and Increase in Deaths, Fewer Marriages and Divorces
item.description: From January to September 2026, Tajikistan registered 175,800 births, a 2.5% decrease from the previous year. Deaths increased by 3.3% to 26,200. Marriages fell by 3.6% to 49,983, while divorces dropped by 14% to 5,397. The increase in deaths was observed across all regions, with Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Province showing the largest relative rise.
